questions.q: What is a standard receipt in Oracle Fusion Receivables?
options: A rebate from a vendor with no link to any customer
A payment from a customer that gets applied against their open transactions
A journal entry created automatically at period close
A report listing every open invoice in the system
questions.explain: A standard receipt is money received from a customer and applied, fully or partially, against their open transactions.

questions.q: Which field on a receipt determines the GL accounts used and the remittance bank account tied to the payment?
options: The receipt number
The customer site
The receipt method
The transaction type
questions.explain: The receipt method points to the accounting rules and remittance bank account, making it the most important field on a receipt.

questions.q: Put the standard receipt lifecycle in the correct order.
options: Cleared, Remitted, Applied, Entered
Entered, Applied, Remitted, Cleared
Applied, Entered, Cleared, Remitted
Remitted, Entered, Cleared, Applied
questions.explain: A receipt is entered as unapplied, applied against open transactions, remitted to the bank, and finally cleared once funds settle.

questions.q: On the Create Receipt page, what can a clerk do in the same pass as entering the receipt?
options: Only print a customer statement
Search for the customer's open transactions and apply the receipt against them
Close the accounting period
Reverse a prior period's journal entries
questions.explain: The Create Receipt page lets a clerk search for open transactions and apply the receipt amount, fully or partially, in the same step.

questions.q: Why might a receipt method skip the separate 'remitted' accounting step and move straight toward cleared?
options: Because the receipt amount was zero
Because the customer requested it in writing
Because the receipt method is configured for 'no clearance,' trusting deposited funds are good
Because Receivables cannot support a remitted status
questions.explain: A receipt method configured with a no-clearance method skips holding funds in a separate clearing account, posting the cash as settled immediately.
